questions.q: In the discovery pipeline plan, what problem does the Glue Crawler specifically solve?
options: It scans the raw files and infers their schema so Athena knows how to query them, without anyone hand-writing a CREATE TABLE statement
It deletes files in S3 that don't match an expected naming convention
It runs the SQL queries that answer the stakeholder's question
It physically copies the CSV files into a new, faster storage format
questions.explain: The crawler's job is schema inference and cataloging — registering a table definition that points at the S3 files, not querying or transforming them.

questions.q: What does the Glue Data Catalog actually store?
options: Metadata — table names, column names, and data types — that points at files still sitting in S3
The Athena query history for the account
A full copy of every row from the raw CSV files
The IAM permissions for every AWS service in the account
questions.explain: The Catalog is metadata only; the actual data never leaves S3 in this pipeline.

questions.q: Why is Athena a good fit for this project's one-off question?
options: It's serverless and billed per terabyte scanned, so there's no idle infrastructure cost for a question asked once
It automatically rewrites CSV files into Parquet before every query
It requires a dedicated cluster that must be provisioned in advance
It can only query data that has already been loaded into Redshift
questions.explain: Athena's pay-per-query, serverless model matches a single ad hoc question far better than provisioning a cluster or warehouse.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when would a Glue ETL job and Redshift actually earn their cost for Northfield?
options: Glue ETL and Redshift are required for any Athena query to work
As soon as there is more than one CSV file in the raw zone
Once there's a recurring workload — a dataset queried repeatedly by multiple people, not a single one-time question
Only after the company stops using S3 entirely
questions.explain: The lesson frames ETL + Redshift as the right answer for a repeatable, recurring reporting need — not for a single ad hoc question.

questions.q: What does "done" look like for this lesson's plan, by the end of Lesson 6?
options: The raw CSV files have been deleted from S3 and replaced with a Glue ETL output
A Glue Crawler has cataloged the raw files as a table, and a simple SELECT * query in Athena proves the whole chain works
A Redshift cluster has been provisioned and loaded with the order data
The Operations Manager's exact question has already been fully answered
questions.explain: Lesson 6 proves the pipeline works end to end with a simple query; the stakeholder's actual question is answered in Lesson 7.
